title: Level 4 (Expert) - A-8
notes:
West's opening club lead should be won as a spade shift would not be welcome. South's best chance is to hope to take 4 heart tricks as well as the ♠A, 2 diamond tricks, and 2 club tricks.

South should lead a heart towards dummy and, when West follows low, play the ♥10 from North. On the given lie of the cards, the ♥10 will hold and a long heart can easily be developed. The ♦K will act as a dummy entry to the long heart.

It may seem intuitive to play the ♥8 on the first round of the suit, playing West for 3 hearts including the ♥9 and either the ♥Q or ♥J. Playing the ♥10 will also work on this distribution of the cards. Playing the ♥10 will be necessary if West started with 4 hearts including the ♥Q and ♥J.

If West plays a heart honour on the first round of the suit, North wins the trick and the other heart honour is cashed. South must decide whether to continue with the ♥10, hoping to pin the ♥9, or with a small heart, hoping West started with 3 hearts including both the ♥Q and ♥J.

The above lie of the cards is the only case in which exiting a low heart will work. Exiting the ♥10 will succeed when West began with 4 hearts including both the ♥Q and ♥J and when West began with 3 hearts including the ♥9 and either the ♥Q or ♥J. Therefore, it is correct to lead the ♥10 on the third round of the suit.
